questions.title: An inspection trolley on an inclined rail
questions.subtopic: An inspection trolley on an inclined rail
questions.stem: A motorized inspection trolley of mass $30.0\,\mathrm{kg}$ moves up a rail inclined at $5.00^\circ$ to the horizontal. Rolling and aerodynamic resistance have resultant magnitude $F_r=bv^2$, opposite to the motion. The motor transfers $80.0\%$ of its electrical input power to mechanical power. At a steady uphill speed of $3.00\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, input power is $300\,\mathrm W$. Take $g=9.81\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.

sourceAnchors.focus: An inspection trolley on an inclined rail

questions.changeNotes: New inclined inspection system, efficiency and gravity; uses force balances in opposite directions and a high-speed limiting law instead of the source car graph.
questions.cognitiveDemand: Link physical models, interpret conditions and justify the result.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Determine $b$ and express its unit using fundamental SI units.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Calculate the electrical input power required for a steady uphill speed of $6.00\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: The trolley is now allowed to roll downhill with its motor disengaged. Determine its terminal speed under the same resistance model.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: For very large uphill speeds, explain how the steady speed changes when electrical input power is multiplied by eight. State the approximation required.

steps.text: Steady mechanical power is $0.800(300)=240\,\mathrm W$, so driving force is $240/3=80.0\,\mathrm N$. Marking guidance: credit a valid subsequent method after an earlier arithmetic or graph-reading error; do not penalize the same numerical error twice. Require a correct physical model and units, and allow consistent use of rounded intermediate values.
$b=6.04\,\mathrm{kg\,m^{-1}}$. Since $F=bv^2$, units are $(\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-2}})/(\mathrm{m^2s^{-2}})=\mathrm{kg\,m^{-1}}$.
At $6.00\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, gravitational force is still $25.650\,\mathrm N$, while resistance is $b(6.00)^2=217.400\,\mathrm N$.
Mechanical power is $(25.650+217.400)(6.00)=1458.30\,\mathrm W$; divide by efficiency.
Input power is $1.82\times10^3\,\mathrm W$ to three significant figures. It is not eight times $300\,\mathrm W$ because the gravitational term scales only linearly with speed.
At terminal speed, $bv^2=mg\sin5.00^\circ$.
If $bv^2\gg mg\sin5^\circ$, the required mechanical power is approximately $bv^3$.
With unchanged efficiency, $v\propto P_{\rm in}^{1/3}$; multiplying power by eight approximately doubles steady speed.

questions.answerSummary: (a) $b=6.04\,\mathrm{kg\,m^{-1}}$. Since $F=bv^2$, units are $(\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-2}})/(\mathrm{m^2s^{-2}})=\mathrm{kg\,m^{-1}}$.; (b) Input power is $1.82\times10^3\,\mathrm W$ to three significant figures. It is not eight times $300\,\mathrm W$ because the gravitational term scales only linearly with speed.; (c) $v=\sqrt{25.650/6.03890}=2.06\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ downhill.; (d) With unchanged efficiency, $v\propto P_{\rm in}^{1/3}$; multiplying power by eight approximately doubles steady speed.

questions.stem: A probe of negligible mass moves in a circular orbit of radius $r_1=7.20\times10^7\,\mathrm m$ around an isolated spherical planet, with orbital period $6.00\,\mathrm h$. A second probe moves in a circular orbit of radius $r_2=1.60r_1$. There is no significant atmospheric drag. Use $G=6.67\times10^{-11}\,\mathrm{N\,m^2kg^{-2}}$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Determine the planet mass from the first orbit.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Determine the second probe orbital period.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Calculate $\phi(r_2)-\phi(r_1)$ and the magnitude of the mean radial field between these radii, defined by $\langle g\rangle=[\phi(r_2)-\phi(r_1)]/(r_2-r_1)$.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Show that the local field magnitude equals this mean at radius $\sqrt{r_1r_2}$, and determine that radius.

steps.text: Equate gravitational and centripetal acceleration: $GM/r_1^2=4\pi^2r_1/T_1^2$. Marking guidance: credit a valid subsequent method after an earlier arithmetic or graph-reading error; do not penalize the same numerical error twice. Require a correct physical model and units, and allow consistent use of rounded intermediate values.
$M=4.74\times10^{26}\,\mathrm{kg}$.
For the same central mass, $T_2/T_1=(r_2/r_1)^{3/2}=1.60^{3/2}$.
$T_2=12.1\,\mathrm h$ to three significant figures.
$\phi=-GM/r$, so $\Delta\phi=GM(1/r_1-1/r_2)>0$.
$\Delta\phi=1.64\times10^8\,\mathrm{J\,kg^{-1}}$.
$\langle g\rangle=\Delta\phi/(0.60r_1)=3.81\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. The actual field direction is inward.
$\langle g\rangle=GM[(r_2-r_1)/(r_1r_2)]/(r_2-r_1)=GM/(r_1r_2)$. Equating to $GM/r^2$ gives $r=\sqrt{r_1r_2}$.
$r=9.11\times10^7\,\mathrm m$. It is the geometric, rather than arithmetic, mean radius.

questions.answerSummary: (a) $M=4.74\times10^{26}\,\mathrm{kg}$.; (b) $T_2=12.1\,\mathrm h$ to three significant figures.; (c) $\langle g\rangle=\Delta\phi/(0.60r_1)=3.81\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. The actual field direction is inward.; (d) $r=9.11\times10^7\,\mathrm m$. It is the geometric, rather than arithmetic, mean radius.

questions.title: Separating background and nuclear decay
questions.stem:
An activated sample contains a parent nuclide P that decays to a stable daughter D. Initially no D is present. Laboratory model count rates at times $0$, $3.00$ and $6.00$ days are $318$, $168$ and $93.0\,\mathrm{min^{-1}}$. The observed rate is a single exponential plus a constant background. Detector calibration shows that $15.0\%$ of parent decays are recorded, including all geometric and detection effects.

Each parent decay releases a total of $550\,\mathrm{keV}$ as gamma radiation, either directly or in a two-photon cascade. Three possible photon energies are $210$, $340$ and $550\,\mathrm{keV}$. Use $1\,\mathrm{eV}=1.602\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm J$ and one day $=86400\,\mathrm s$.
questions.changeNotes: New unknown-background inverse problem, calibrated decay efficiency and a direct/cascade gamma-energy account; no gold data copied.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Determine the background rate and the parent half-life. Show how the equal time intervals constrain the background.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Determine the decay constant in $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$ and the initial number of parent nuclei.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Determine the number of daughter nuclei and the total emitted gamma energy after $9.00$ days.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Draw a minimal energy-level diagram that can account for the three gamma energies. Explain why this is consistent with quantized nuclear energies.

steps.text: For background $B$, the common three-day decay factor requires $(168-B)^2=(318-B)(93-B)$. Marking guidance: credit a valid subsequent method after an earlier arithmetic or graph-reading error; do not penalize the same numerical error twice. Require a correct physical model and units, and allow consistent use of rounded intermediate values.
This gives $B=18.0\,\mathrm{min^{-1}}$, so corrected rates are $300$, $150$ and $75.0\,\mathrm{min^{-1}}$.
The corrected rate halves in each $3.00$-day interval; $t_{1/2}=3.00$ days.
$A_0=(300/60)/0.150=33.333\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}$ and $N_0=A_0/\lambda=1.25\times10^7$. Use unrounded $\lambda$ in this calculation.
After three half-lives, $N_P=N_0/8$ and $N_D=7N_0/8$.
$N_D=1.09\times10^7$ daughter nuclei.
Total gamma energy is $N_D(550\times10^3)(1.602\times10^{-19})=9.61\times10^{-7}\,\mathrm J$. A two-photon cascade still carries total energy $550\,\mathrm{keV}$ per decay.

Draw levels at $0$, $340$ and $550\,\mathrm{keV}$, with downward arrows $550\to0$, $550\to340$ and $340\to0$. The two-step route emits $210+340=550\,\mathrm{keV}$. An intermediate level at $210\,\mathrm{keV}$ is an equivalent minimal arrangement.
Discrete photon energies correspond to fixed differences between allowed nuclear energy levels, rather than a continuum of possible nuclear energies.

questions.answerSummary: (a) The corrected rate halves in each $3.00$-day interval; $t_{1/2}=3.00$ days.; (b) $A_0=(300/60)/0.150=33.333\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}$ and $N_0=A_0/\lambda=1.25\times10^7$. Use unrounded $\lambda$ in this calculation.; (c) Total gamma energy is $N_D(550\times10^3)(1.602\times10^{-19})=9.61\times10^{-7}\,\mathrm J$. A two-photon cascade still carries total energy $550\,\mathrm{keV}$ per decay.; (d) Discrete photon energies correspond to fixed differences between allowed nuclear energy levels, rather than a continuum of possible nuclear energies.

questions.title: Finite thermal bodies and maximum work
questions.subtopic: Finite thermal bodies and maximum work
questions.stem:
Two solid blocks, each of constant heat capacity $C=100\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, start at $300\,\mathrm K$ and $450\,\mathrm K$. They are thermally insulated from their surroundings; useful work can be transferred to an external ideal work store in the second arrangement. No phase changes occur. For either block, use the supplied relation
$$\Delta S=C\ln(T_f/T_i).$$
In a second arrangement, a reversible engine operates between the two blocks, extracting work until their temperatures are equal. The engine returns to its initial state.

sourceAnchors.focus: Finite thermal bodies and maximum work

questions.changeNotes: Replaces a qualitative microstate example with finite bodies and a supplied entropy model; requires distinguishing energy conservation from reversible maximum work.
questions.cognitiveDemand: Link physical models, interpret conditions and justify the result.

verification.method: Author calculation, dimensional and limiting-case checks
verification.notes: Executable values for every numerical part are named P2Q04 in hl-b-author-checks.json; limiting cases and units are checked in the solutions.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the final temperature if the blocks are simply placed in direct thermal contact, with no work extracted.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Calculate their total entropy change in direct contact and explain its sign.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: For the reversible-engine arrangement, determine the common final temperature and the maximum work extracted.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: A proposed engine would leave both blocks at $300\,\mathrm K$ and deliver the entire reduction in block internal energy as work, without any other change. Explain why energy conservation alone does not validate this proposal.

steps.text: No energy leaves, so $C(T_f-300)=C(450-T_f)$. Marking guidance: credit a valid subsequent method after an earlier arithmetic or graph-reading error; do not penalize the same numerical error twice. Require a correct physical model and units, and allow consistent use of rounded intermediate values.
$T_f=375\,\mathrm K$.
Direct heat transfer through a finite temperature difference is irreversible. The isolated system entropy increases, consistently with the second law.
Reversibility requires zero total entropy change: $\ln(T_f/300)+\ln(T_f/450)=0$, hence $T_f^2=300(450)$.
$T_f=367\,\mathrm K$ to three significant figures.
$W_{\max}=C[300+450-2\sqrt{300(450)}]=1.52\times10^3\,\mathrm J$. The reversible final temperature is below the direct-contact arithmetic mean.
Both blocks at $300\,\mathrm K$ would give total entropy change $100\ln(300/450)=-40.5\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$.

With no other change, the engine cannot compensate this entropy decrease. Although a first-law energy balance could be written, the proposal violates the second law and exceeds the reversible maximum work.

questions.answerSummary: (a) $T_f=375\,\mathrm K$.; (b) Direct heat transfer through a finite temperature difference is irreversible. The isolated system entropy increases, consistently with the second law.; (c) $W_{\max}=C[300+450-2\sqrt{300(450)}]=1.52\times10^3\,\mathrm J$. The reversible final temperature is below the direct-contact arithmetic mean.; (d) With no other change, the engine cannot compensate this entropy decrease. Although a first-law energy balance could be written, the proposal violates the second law and exceeds the reversible maximum work.

questions.title: An acoustic echo and a reflecting boundary
questions.subtopic: An acoustic echo and a reflecting boundary
questions.stem:
A small vehicle approaches a stationary vertical wall. Its onboard source emits $40.0\,\mathrm{kHz}$ sound and its receiver detects a reflected frequency of $43.0\,\mathrm{kHz}$. The speed of sound in air is $343\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Treat reflection at the wall as preserving the frequency in the wall frame.

In a separate stationary arrangement, a sound source S and detector D are $1.20\,\mathrm m$ apart, both $0.450\,\mathrm m$ above a flat water surface. Sound reaches D directly and by reflection at P, midway horizontally between S and D. There is no phase change of the pressure wave at reflection. The sound speed in water is $1480\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, and both media are non-dispersive.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Determine the speed of the approaching vehicle, accounting for both stages of the reflected Doppler shift.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: For the stationary arrangement, determine the lowest positive frequency producing destructive interference of the direct and reflected pressure waves at D.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Use wave refraction to decide whether a propagating transmitted ray in water exists for the ray SP at the same incident angle. Show your angular calculation.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Within the stated non-dispersive model, can changing only the frequency restore a transmitted ray at that incident angle? Explain.

steps.text: The wall receives $f_w=fv/(v-u)$ because the source approaches it. Marking guidance: credit a valid subsequent method after an earlier arithmetic or graph-reading error; do not penalize the same numerical error twice. Require a correct physical model and units, and allow consistent use of rounded intermediate values.
The moving receiver then detects $f_r=f_w(v+u)/v=f(v+u)/(v-u)$.
The reflected length is $2\sqrt{0.600^2+0.450^2}=1.50\,\mathrm m$; path difference is $0.300\,\mathrm m$.
With no reflection phase reversal, the lowest positive destructive frequency has path difference $\lambda/2$, so $\lambda=0.600\,\mathrm m$.
$f=343/0.600=572\,\mathrm{Hz}$ to three significant figures.
Incident angle to the normal is $\theta_i=\tan^{-1}(0.600/0.450)=53.1^\circ$.
The critical angle is $\sin^{-1}(v_{\rm air}/v_{\rm water})=\sin^{-1}(343/1480)=13.4^\circ$.
Since $53.1^\circ>13.4^\circ$, the geometric-acoustics model gives total internal reflection and no propagating refracted ray. Equivalently the required refracted sine would exceed one.

No. The critical angle depends on the speed ratio, which is frequency-independent under the stated non-dispersive assumption. Frequency changes the interference condition, not this transmission condition.

questions.answerSummary: (a) $u=v(f_r-f)/(f_r+f)=343(43.0-40.0)/(43.0+40.0)=12.4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.; (b) $f=343/0.600=572\,\mathrm{Hz}$ to three significant figures.; (c) Since $53.1^\circ>13.4^\circ$, the geometric-acoustics model gives total internal reflection and no propagating refracted ray. Equivalently the required refracted sine would exceed one.; (d) No. The critical angle depends on the speed ratio, which is frequency-independent under the stated non-dispersive assumption. Frequency changes the interference condition, not this transmission condition.

questions.title: An ion velocity selector and magnetic analyser
questions.subtopic: An ion velocity selector and magnetic analyser
questions.stem:
Singly positive ions are accelerated from rest through $4.20\,\mathrm{kV}$. They enter crossed uniform fields: electric field $E=2.40\times10^4\,\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$ downwards and magnetic field of magnitude $0.0800\,\mathrm T$. Selected ions travel horizontally to the right without deflection.

After the selector, they enter a region containing only a uniform magnetic field of $0.200\,\mathrm T$ into the page. They follow a semicircle and hit a detector in the entry plane. Use $e=1.602\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm C$ and $1\,\mathrm u=1.66\times10^{-27}\,\mathrm{kg}$. Motion is non-relativistic.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Determine the selected speed and the required direction of the selector magnetic field.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Determine the selected ion mass and its approximate nucleon number, taking nuclear mass to be approximately $A\,\mathrm u$.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Determine the separation of the detector impact point from the analyser entry point.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Ions of a heavier isotope with the same charge are accelerated through the same potential difference. Explain whether they pass the selector, and toward which plate they initially deflect.

steps.text: $qE=qvB$ gives $v=E/B=3.00\times10^5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Marking guidance: credit a valid subsequent method after an earlier arithmetic or graph-reading error; do not penalize the same numerical error twice. Require a correct physical model and units, and allow consistent use of rounded intermediate values.
The electric force is downward. The magnetic force on a positive ion moving right must be upward, requiring magnetic field into the page.
$qV=mv^2/2$ gives $m=2eV/v^2$.
$m/\mathrm u=9.007$, so the approximate nucleon number is $A=9$.
The magnetic force supplies centripetal force: $evB=mv^2/r$, so $r=mv/(eB)$.
$r=0.140\,\mathrm m$.
The displacement after a semicircle in the entry plane is a diameter, $2r=0.280\,\mathrm m$, above the entry point for the stated field direction.
At fixed $qV$, speed is proportional to $m^{-1/2}$, so a heavier isotope is slower than the selected speed and is not transmitted undeflected.
Its upward magnetic force $qvB$ is smaller than the unchanged downward electric force $qE$; it initially deflects down toward the negative plate.

questions.answerSummary: (a) The electric force is downward. The magnetic force on a positive ion moving right must be upward, requiring magnetic field into the page.; (b) $m/\mathrm u=9.007$, so the approximate nucleon number is $A=9$.; (c) The displacement after a semicircle in the entry plane is a diameter, $2r=0.280\,\mathrm m$, above the entry point for the stated field direction.; (d) Its upward magnetic force $qvB$ is smaller than the unchanged downward electric force $qE$; it initially deflects down toward the negative plate.

questions.title: Reversed event order and causality
questions.stem:
In inertial frame S, event P is a flash at $x=0$, $ct=0$. Event Q is a separately programmed flash at $x=1200\,\mathrm m$, $ct=900\,\mathrm m$. Frame S′ moves at $+0.800c$ relative to S and its origin coincides with P. Use
$$x'=\gamma(x-\beta ct),\qquad ct'=\gamma(ct-\beta x),\qquad \gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}.$$
Use the convention $(\Delta s)^2=(c\Delta t)^2-(\Delta x)^2$.
questions.changeNotes: New flashes, explicit negative time coordinate and a causal-signalling test; derives the simultaneous separation as an invariant check.
questions.cognitiveDemand: Link physical models, interpret conditions and justify the result.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the invariant interval between P and Q and classify their separation.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Calculate the S′ coordinates of Q and state which flash occurs first in that frame.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Determine the speed of a frame in which the flashes are simultaneous and the spatial separation of the flashes in that frame.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Explain why the reversed time order creates no causal paradox, and why Q cannot have been triggered by a signal emitted at P.

steps.text: $(\Delta s)^2=900^2-1200^2$. Marking guidance: credit a valid subsequent method after an earlier arithmetic or graph-reading error; do not penalize the same numerical error twice. Require a correct physical model and units, and allow consistent use of rounded intermediate values.
$(\Delta s)^2=-6.30\times10^5\,\mathrm{m^2}<0$, so the separation is spacelike.
$ct^{\prime}_Q=(5/3)(900-0.800\times1200)=-100\,\mathrm m$. Since P remains at $ct^{\prime}=0$, Q occurs first in S′.
Simultaneity requires $900-\beta(1200)=0$, so the frame speed is $+0.750c$.
With $\Delta ct^{\prime\prime}=0$, invariance gives $\Delta x^{\prime\prime}=\sqrt{630000}=794\,\mathrm m$. Direct Lorentz transformation gives the same value.
In S, light travels only $900\,\mathrm m$ during the time between the events, less than their $1200\,\mathrm m$ separation.
A signal from P to Q would require speed $\Delta x/\Delta t=(4/3)c>c$, so no allowed causal signal connects them.
Spacelike events have no causal ordering enforced by a light-speed-limited influence. Different inertial observers may reverse their time order without reversing any actual cause and effect.

questions.answerSummary: (a) $(\Delta s)^2=-6.30\times10^5\,\mathrm{m^2}<0$, so the separation is spacelike.; (b) $ct^{\prime}_Q=(5/3)(900-0.800\times1200)=-100\,\mathrm m$. Since P remains at $ct^{\prime}=0$, Q occurs first in S′.; (c) With $\Delta ct^{\prime\prime}=0$, invariance gives $\Delta x^{\prime\prime}=\sqrt{630000}=794\,\mathrm m$. Direct Lorentz transformation gives the same value.; (d) Spacelike events have no causal ordering enforced by a light-speed-limited influence. Different inertial observers may reverse their time order without reversing any actual cause and effect.

questions.title: A main-sequence energy budget
questions.stem:
A main-sequence star is modelled as a blackbody with luminosity $8.00\times10^{26}\,\mathrm W$, effective surface temperature $7200\,\mathrm K$ and mass $1.40M_\odot$, where $M_\odot=2.00\times10^{30}\,\mathrm{kg}$. Its initial hydrogen mass fraction is $0.700$. In this simplified lifetime model, $12.0\%$ of that hydrogen mass can undergo fusion, converting $0.700\%$ of the consumed hydrogen rest mass into energy. Neutrinos carry away $2.00\%$ of the released energy; the rest supplies the stated luminosity.

For a reaction-rate estimate, use $26.7\,\mathrm{MeV}$ total energy released per completed four-proton fusion chain. Use $\sigma=5.67\times10^{-8}\,\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}K^{-4}}$, $c=3.00\times10^8\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $1\,\mathrm{eV}=1.602\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm J$ and one year $=3.15576\times10^7\,\mathrm s$.
questions.changeNotes: New stellar model separates accessible fuel, mass-conversion efficiency and neutrino losses; quantitative rate and hydrostatic-feedback tasks use no source solar numbers.
questions.cognitiveDemand: Link physical models, interpret conditions and justify the result.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Determine the stellar radius.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Estimate the model main-sequence lifetime, assuming constant luminosity and the stated accessible fuel fraction.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Determine the number of completed fusion chains per second needed to supply the luminosity.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Calculate the rate of stellar mass loss due to all the escaping radiation and neutrinos. Then explain how a small increase in core fusion rate can be moderated by hydrostatic feedback in a stable main-sequence star.

steps.text: Use $L=4\pi R^2\sigma T^4$. Marking guidance: credit a valid subsequent method after an earlier arithmetic or graph-reading error; do not penalize the same numerical error twice. Require a correct physical model and units, and allow consistent use of rounded intermediate values.
Accessible hydrogen mass is $0.700(0.120)(1.40)(2.00\times10^{30})=2.352\times10^{29}\,\mathrm{kg}$.
Energy available to the photon luminosity is $0.980(0.00700)(2.352\times10^{29})c^2=1.45212\times10^{44}\,\mathrm J$.
$t=E/L=1.81516\times10^{17}\,\mathrm s=5.75\times10^9$ years. This estimate assumes constant luminosity, composition/fuel accessibility as specified and the given mass-conversion fraction.
Photon energy available per completed chain is $0.980(26.7\times10^6)(1.602\times10^{-19})\,\mathrm J$.
Number of chains per second is $L/E_{\rm photon,chain}=1.91\times10^{38}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}$. Do not treat the neutrino fraction as part of the observed photon luminosity.
All escaping power is $L/0.980$, so $\dot m=L/(0.980c^2)=9.07\times10^9\,\mathrm{kg\,s^{-1}}$.
An enhanced fusion rate heats the core and raises its pressure, tending to expand the star/core against gravity.

Expansion cools the core and reduces the temperature-sensitive fusion rate, providing negative feedback around hydrostatic equilibrium. Accept an equivalent physically consistent account of pressure, gravity and temperature.

questions.answerSummary: (a) $R=\sqrt{8.00\times10^{26}/[4\pi(5.67\times10^{-8})(7200)^4]}=6.46\times10^8\,\mathrm m$.; (b) $t=E/L=1.81516\times10^{17}\,\mathrm s=5.75\times10^9$ years. This estimate assumes constant luminosity, composition/fuel accessibility as specified and the given mass-conversion fraction.; (c) Number of chains per second is $L/E_{\rm photon,chain}=1.91\times10^{38}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}$. Do not treat the neutrino fraction as part of the observed photon luminosity.; (d) Expansion cools the core and reduces the temperature-sensitive fusion rate, providing negative feedback around hydrostatic equilibrium. Accept an equivalent physically consistent account of pressure, gravity and temperature.

questions.title: Quantifying electromagnetic damping
questions.stem:
A light rectangular coil attached to a horizontal spring oscillates along the $x$ direction. The total moving mass is $0.0800\,\mathrm{kg}$ and the spring constant is $12.0\,\mathrm{N\,m^{-1}}$. The initial amplitude is $0.0400\,\mathrm m$. Mechanical friction is negligible.

The coil has $200$ turns, each of area $4.00\times10^{-4}\,\mathrm{m^2}$. A static magnetic field is perpendicular to the coil, with constant spatial gradient $dB/dx=8.00\,\mathrm{T\,m^{-1}}$ across the operating region. Flux linkage is $NA B(x)$, where $x$ is the coil centre. The circuit resistance is $20.0\,\Omega$; self-inductance is negligible.

For weak damping with force $F=-bv$, use the supplied amplitude envelope
$$a(t)=a_0e^{-bt/(2m)}.$$
Use the undamped period to estimate elapsed time for a given number of cycles.
questions.changeNotes: Changes a qualitative spring-magnet setup into a translating coil in a specified field gradient; derives damping from power and tests a quantitative amplitude envelope.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the undamped period and initial maximum speed.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Calculate the initial maximum induced emf.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Using the rate of electrical energy dissipation and energy conservation, show that the magnetic damping coefficient is $b=(NA\,dB/dx)^2/R$. Calculate $b$ and justify the force direction.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Estimate the fraction of initial oscillation energy remaining after ten cycles. Explain the limiting effect of disconnecting the external circuit.

steps.text: $T=2\pi\sqrt{m/k}=0.513\,\mathrm s$. Marking guidance: credit a valid subsequent method after an earlier arithmetic or graph-reading error; do not penalize the same numerical error twice. Require a correct physical model and units, and allow consistent use of rounded intermediate values.
$\omega=\sqrt{k/m}=12.247\,\mathrm{rad\,s^{-1}}$ and $v_{\max}=\omega a_0=0.490\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.
Faraday law gives $|\varepsilon|=|d(NAB)/dt|=NA|dB/dx|\,|v|$.
$P_R=\varepsilon^2/R=(NA\,dB/dx)^2v^2/R$. This energy is taken from the oscillator; $Fv=-P_R$, so $F=-[(NA\,dB/dx)^2/R]v$.
The force opposes velocity, as required by energy conservation and Lenz law. A force in the velocity direction would increase mechanical energy while also heating the resistor without a source.
$E\propto a^2$, so $E(t)/E_0=e^{-bt/m}$ and $t\approx10T=5.1302\,\mathrm s$.
$E/E_0=e^{-(0.02048)(5.1302)/0.0800}=0.269$. The small ratio $b/(2m\omega)\approx0.0105$ supports the weak-damping period approximation.

For an open circuit, $R\to\infty$, induced current and magnetic damping tend to zero. A changing flux can still produce an emf, but there is negligible Joule energy dissipation in this idealized limit.

questions.answerSummary: (a) $\omega=\sqrt{k/m}=12.247\,\mathrm{rad\,s^{-1}}$ and $v_{\max}=\omega a_0=0.490\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.; (b) $\varepsilon_{\max}=(200)(4.00\times10^{-4})(8.00)(0.489898)=0.314\,\mathrm V$.; (c) The force opposes velocity, as required by energy conservation and Lenz law. A force in the velocity direction would increase mechanical energy while also heating the resistor without a source.; (d) For an open circuit, $R\to\infty$, induced current and magnetic damping tend to zero. A changing flux can still produce an emf, but there is negligible Joule energy dissipation in this idealized limit.
